figures.caption: Figure 2. Aggregate performance by dimensionality. For each d ∈ {5, 7, 10}, bars show Mean Total SHD averaged over all environments (K) and sample sizes (T ), for ECR-Net (gold) and Static VAR (blue). Error bars denote ±1 standard deviation across runs.

Figure 3. Aggregate impact of non-stationarity. For each K ∈ {3, 4, 5, 10}, bars show Mean Total SHD averaged over all dimensionalities (d) and sample sizes (T ), for ECR-Net (gold) and Static VAR (blue). Error bars denote ±1 standard deviation.
Figure 4. ECR-Net Advantage Heatmap: Mean SHD Reduction (Static SHD − ECR SHD) averaged across sample sizes. Brighter cells indicate greater advantage in high d, high K regimes.
Figure 5. ECR-Net Mean Total SHD (averaged over sample sizes) across varying number of variables (d) and environments (K). Lighter colors indicate better performance (lower SHD).
Figure 6. Effect of Sample Size on Mean Total SHD for d = 10,K = 10. ECR-Net remains stable across increasing T , indicating structural rather than data-driven advantage.
